name: Self-Rewarding Language Models
authors: Weizhe Yuan, Richard Yuanzhe Pang, Kyunghyun Cho, Xian Li, Sainbayar Sukhbaatar, Jing Xu, Jason Weston (Meta AI / NYU); lead affiliation Meta
code_url: No official code release from authors; method reproduced in community implementations (e.g., HuggingFace/Oxen.ai). Authors did not release official training code or model weights.
reflection_type: learned-critic-model (the model itself acts as an LLM-as-a-Judge reward model / self-critic); the judge ability is itself improved by training, so it is a self-generated learned critic rather than a separate frozen reward model
feedback_source: self-generated (LLM-as-a-Judge: the same model assigns scalar rewards 0-5 to its own candidate responses via an additive 5-criteria scoring prompt). No external tool, unit test, or ground-truth oracle is used for the reward signal; a small human-authored seed set (IFT + EFT) bootstraps the judge.
iteration_structure: iterative-refine across training rounds (population of model generations) within an Iterative DPO framework: starting from seed model M0, each iteration generates self-instruction data, self-judges it to build preference pairs, and trains the next model via DPO (M1 -> M2 -> M3); 3 iterations run.
reflection_object: model weights (the reflective/judgment signal is distilled into the next iteration's parameters via DPO). The proximate object reflected on is the model's own output content / candidate responses (judged by LLM-as-a-Judge), but the persistent locus of improvement is the weights — both the policy and the embedded reward/judge capability.
learning_locus: gradient_weight_update (preference data generated by self-judging is consumed by DPO, updating model weights each iteration).
requires_training: DPO/preference (Iterative DPO: each iteration builds a preference dataset from self-rewarded pairs and runs DPO; seeded by SFT on IFT+EFT data).
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge (the policy model itself, via LLM-as-a-Judge prompting, provides the reward). No separate trained reward model or external verifiable reward; the judge improves alongside the policy across iterations.
distillation_target: model-weights (self-generated preference judgments are distilled into the next iteration's parameters via DPO; no external memory or skill library is produced).
emergent_vs_engineered: scaffold-engineered: the self-rewarding loop is an explicitly engineered pipeline (LLM-as-a-Judge additive-scoring prompt + Iterative DPO), not an RL-emergent reflective behavior. However, the improvement of the reward-modeling ability across iterations is an emergent training-dynamics effect within that engineered scaffold.
memory_type: none (no explicit episodic memory, scratchpad, or skill library). 'Memory' is implicit: experience is absorbed into model weights and the growing AIFT preference datasets used for the next iteration.
memory_persistence: cross-task / cross-iteration in the sense that learning accumulates in weights across training rounds; there is no within-episode or cross-session inference-time memory store.
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a (no inference-time memory). At the data level, each iteration appends newly self-generated and self-judged preference pairs to form the training set (AIFT(M1)=3,964 pairs to train M2; AIFT(M2)=6,942 pairs to train M3); pairs are selected as highest-vs-lowest scored among candidates (append-and-select per round).
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level / response-level: the LLM-as-a-Judge assigns a single additive 0-5 score to a whole candidate response (criteria: relevance, coverage, usefulness, clarity, expertise); no step-level, token-level, or block-level credit assignment.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task: the method is an offline training procedure that improves the model across newly generated instruction-following prompts and iterations; it is not within-task in-context refinement of a single response.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only / training-time improvement: there is no mid-trajectory recovery or post-hoc revision of a single answer at inference; the model improves future behavior via weight updates. The DPO loss pushes away from lower-scored (worse) self-generations.
task_domains: general-alignment / instruction-following (primary); also evaluated on QA/reasoning and standard NLP benchmarks (math GSM8K, MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, etc.) and MT-Bench multi-turn categories (math, coding, roleplay, writing).
benchmarks: AlpacaEval 2.0 (win rate vs GPT-4 Turbo), MT-Bench, head-to-head GPT-4 judged win rates on 256 IFT test prompts, human evaluation, and 9 NLP benchmarks: ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, SIQA, PIQA, GSM8K, MMLU, OBQA, NQ. Reward-modeling accuracy measured on a held-out Open Assistant preference evaluation set.
headline_result: Fine-tuning Llama 2 70B (seeded on Open Assistant) over 3 iterations of self-rewarding Iterative DPO raises AlpacaEval 2.0 win rate vs GPT-4 Turbo from 9.94% (M1) to 15.38% (M2) to 20.44% (M3); the M3 model outperforms Claude 2, Gemini Pro, and GPT-4 0613 on the AlpacaEval 2.0 leaderboard. Reward-modeling pairwise accuracy with humans also improves across iterations (65.1% -> 78.7% -> 80.4% -> 81.7%).
baselines: SFT Baseline (Llama 2 70B fine-tuned on IFT seed data only), the seed model M0, Self-Rewarding iterations M1/M2/M3 against each other, and external leaderboard systems (Claude 2, Gemini Pro, GPT-4 0613, GPT-4 Turbo as the AlpacaEval reference); also IFT-only vs IFT+EFT ablation for the judge.
gains_vs_baseline: AlpacaEval 2.0 win rate vs GPT-4 Turbo: M1 9.94% -> M3 20.44% (about +10.5 points across iterations; each iteration of self-rewarding DPO gives further gains, M2 15.38%). Head-to-head: SFT baseline is on par with M1; M2 beats M1 and SFT; M3 beats M1, M2 and SFT by a large margin. Reward-model pairwise accuracy: SFT/M1 65.1% -> M2-style 78.7% (IFT+EFT effect), and over self-training iterations 65.1% -> 78.7% -> 80.4% -> 81.7%; Spearman corr. 0.253 -> 0.349. MT-Bench overall: SFT 6.85 -> M3 7.25. Standard NLP benchmarks remain comparable to the Llama 2 70B base/SFT (no degradation; e.g., GSM8K M1 60.27 vs SFT 50.72).
compute_cost_profile: Training-side cost: 3 iterations of generation + self-judging + full DPO fine-tuning of a 70B model. Each iteration generates candidate responses (4 per new prompt) and runs the judge 3 times per response (averaged) to assign rewards, then builds preference pairs (AIFT M1 = 3,964 pairs; AIFT M2 = 6,942 pairs) and runs DPO. No quantitative GPU-hour/FLOP cost reported in the paper. At inference the final model is a single standard model with no added pass overhead (the self-rewarding cost is incurred only during training data generation).
known_limitations: Authors call results preliminary: only 3 iterations in a single setting (Llama 2 70B), so scaling laws of iterative self-improvement are unknown and gains may saturate/bottleneck. Observed increase in generation length with known length-quality correlation (possible length bias / reward hacking not ruled out). Potential reward-hacking and shared-bias risk since both the training reward and part of the evaluation use LLM judges (GPT-4 for AlpacaEval, model-as-judge for training), even if different models. No safety evaluation or safety training conducted. Relies on a human-authored seed set (IFT+EFT) to bootstrap the judge.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: self-verify / intrinsic-only for the reward signal: rewards come entirely from the model's own LLM-as-a-Judge with NO ground-truth oracle, external tool, or verifiable reward in the loop. A small human-authored seed set (IFT instructions + EFT judge examples) bootstraps the judge, and GPT-4 is used as an external evaluator at test time (but not as a training signal). This places it in the 'self-verify without oracle labels' regime — distinct from oracle-dependent self-correction methods.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive within scope: unlike intrinsic single-shot self-correction (which Huang et al. find degrades without oracle feedback), here the self-judging signal drives genuine measured gains in BOTH instruction following (AlpacaEval 9.94%->20.44%) and reward-modeling accuracy (65.1%->81.7%) across iterations. Efficacy is amplified because the judge itself is trained/improved (EFT data) and improvement is realized via weight updates rather than in-context revision; long-run efficacy is unverified (only 3 iterations, possible saturation/reward-hacking).
calibration_effect: not-measured: the paper does not report confidence-calibration metrics. Indirect signal: the model's reward-judgment quality (agreement with human rankings, Spearman/Kendall correlation) improves with iterations, but predictive calibration / overconfidence ('reasoning tax') is not evaluated.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (this is a training/self-improvement method, not a failure-attribution or trace-analysis object; it does not classify failure modes or attribute responsible agents/steps).
failure_mode_addressed: Targets the human-feedback bottleneck of frozen reward models in RLHF/DPO (reward model cannot improve during training and is capped at human level). Self-reported risk it may introduce: length-bias / superficial-quality reward hacking and shared-judge-bias (relevant to MAST-style 'superficial self-reflection' / reward-hacking failure modes). It does not address multi-agent coordination failure modes.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new reusable benchmark or dataset released by the authors. Uses existing resources: Open Assistant (seed IFT/EFT and reward-model eval set) and AlpacaEval 2.0 / MT-Bench for evaluation. Self-generated AIFT preference datasets were not publicly released.
builds_on: Iterative DPO (Xu et al., 2023, 'Some things are more cringe than others' / Pairwise Cringe Optimization); DPO (Rafailov et al., 2023); LLM-as-a-Judge (Zheng et al., 2023, MT-Bench); RLHF/InstructGPT (Ouyang et al., 2022); Constitutional AI / RLAIF (Bai et al., 2022); instruction self-creation (Self-Instruct, Wang et al. 2023; Li et al. 2024 Self-Alignment with Instruction Backtranslation). Seed model: Llama 2 70B (Touvron et al., 2023) on Open Assistant (Köpf et al., 2023).
extended_by_or_inspired: Meta-Rewarding Language Models (Wu et al., 2024, arXiv 2407.19594, adds a meta-judge to improve the judge itself); Self-Rewarding correction / self-rewarding reasoning for math (e.g., 'Self-rewarding correction for mathematical reasoning', 2025); CREAM (Consistency Regularized Self-Rewarding, 2024); numerous self-rewarding / label-free RLVR follow-ups (e.g., Co-rewarding 2025) and self-rewarding extensions to vision/text-to-image (Class-Conditional self-reward, 2024). Broadly cited as a foundational self-improvement / self-alignment method.
reasoning_model_native: no: the method predates and does not target o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in reflection. It is an alignment/instruction-following self-improvement method on Llama 2 70B; reflection here is an engineered LLM-as-a-Judge scaffold, not RL-emergent chain-of-thought reflection. Its self-rewarding idea has, however, been adapted in later self-rewarding reasoning work.
on_policy_distillation_link: Strong conceptual link to self-distillation / on-policy improvement: each iteration generates on-policy samples from the current model, self-scores them, and distills the preference signal back into weights via DPO — a self-bootstrapping loop closely related to on-policy self-improvement and skill self-optimization. It is not classic teacher->student distillation (no external teacher); the model is its own teacher and student.
sample_efficiency: 3 training iterations (M1->M2->M3) suffice to reach the reported headline gains; preference data scale ~3,964 pairs (AIFT M1) and ~6,942 pairs (AIFT M2) plus ~3,200 IFT + ~1,775 EFT seed examples. Gains continue across the 3 iterations but the number of iterations to saturation is unknown (authors flag this as future work).
